Between:-
 Deendayal @ Bhure S/O Shri Darau Ahirwar,
 Aged About 28 Years, R/O Nandrayi, P.S
 Pathariya, District Damoh (Madhya Pradesh).

(By Shri S.M. Guru - Advocate)
 And
 State Of Madhya Pradesh Through P.S
 Pathariya, District Damoh (Madhya Pradesh).
 
 (By Shri Dinesh Prasad Patel - Dy. Government Advocate)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No. 671/2022, registered at Police Station Pathariya, District Damoh (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 376, 376(2)(N) and 506 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that incident is said to have occurred on 28.07.2022 and report has been lodged after delay of about 5 months on 01.12.2022.
It is submitted that false story is made out against applicant.
Prosecutrix has stated that she was subjected to forceful intercourse and she was also beaten, however, in MLC, no external or internal injury was found on body or private part of prosecutrix.
It is submitted that prosecutrix is major aged about 35 years.
There was financial dispute between applicant and prosecutrix.
Applicant is innocent and falsely being implicated in the case.
In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: 3. Learned Deputy Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
It is submitted by him that as per 164 statement of prosecutrix, her hands and legs were tied and thereafter, she was subject to rape.
She was badly beaten by applicant.
In view of same, application be dismissed.

4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5.
Prosecutrix is said to have been badly beaten, however, in MLC, no external or internal injury was found.
There is delay in lodging of FIR of about 5 months.
No reasonable explanation has been given for delay.
6. Considering facts and circumstances of the case, bail application filed by applicant is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court for his appearance before the trial court on the dates to be fixed by the trial court.

8. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9. C.C as per rules.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE vkt Deendayal @ Bhure vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173078697/
